title: God is not silent.
paragraphs:
God is not silent.
You’re just not ready for what He’s saying.

Because deep down…
you don’t want an answer that costs you everything.

“Lord, why is this happening?”
“Why is evil winning?”
“Why does it feel like You’re not doing anything?”
But what if heaven is not quiet?
What if the real tension is this:
God has already answered… and you don’t like the answer.

Not from a distance.
From the inside.
He saw injustice everywhere—violence in the streets, corruption in leadership, truth being crushed like dust under sandals.

“O Lord, how long shall I cry for help, and you will not hear? Or cry to you ‘Violence!’ and you will not save?”
— Habakkuk 1:2

You smile in church.
But inside, you’re wrestling.

You see wicked people prosper.
You see faithful people suffer.

You see injustice go viral.
And righteousness go unnoticed.
And somewhere in your chest, a quiet accusation forms:

“Look among the nations, and see; wonder and be astounded. For I am doing a work in your days that you would not believe if told.”
— Habakkuk 1:5
But then He reveals how He is working—

A ruthless nation.
Violent. Proud. Godless.
God was raising them up as an instrument of judgment.
Because Habakkuk wasn’t just struggling with silence anymore.
He was struggling with God’s method.
But only the kind we approve of.
But only in ways that make sense to us.
But not ones that disrupt our comfort, our control, our version of righteousness.

We are not just confused by injustice.
We are implicated in it.
We point fingers at the world.
But Scripture turns the mirror toward us.

“None is righteous, no, not one.” — Romans 3:10
“All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
The violence Habakkuk saw out there—
This is the emotional trigger you didn’t expect:

Because when the light hits your soul…
you realize:
And this is where everything turns.
Because God did not ignore injustice.
He did not sweep sin under heaven’s carpet.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness.” — 1 Peter 2:24
Took the weight of our rebellion.
Every moment we questioned God’s goodness while living in quiet disobedience.
And He was crushed for it.
“But he was pierced for our transgressions; he was crushed for our iniquities… and with his wounds we are healed.” — Isaiah 53:5
He is so just that sin must be punished.
And so merciful that He took that punishment Himself—in Jesus.
So when you ask, “God, why aren’t You doing anything?”
You don’t just admire the cross.
Stop demanding answers while resisting surrender.
Because the same God who shook Habakkuk’s understanding—
“Though the fig tree should not blossom… yet I will rejoice in the Lord; I will take joy in the God of my salvation.” — Habakkuk 3:17–18
God may not answer the way you want.
But He will always reveal who He is.
And that is enough for those who truly seek Him.
Will you keep arguing from a distance?
Or will you surrender up close?
If your heart is stirring right now…
Type “OPEN MY HEART” if you’re ready to stop resisting and start surrendering.
